$comment: The piece manifest. For most projects this and CONTRACT.md are the only files
you write by hand — the two workflow templates read this and need no editing.
1. `owns` globs must be DISJOINT across every piece. Overlap is the one
failure mode parallel agents cannot recover from.
2. A piece must be judgeable ALONE, from the review sheet, by someone who
has not seen the code. If you cannot name the shots that show it, it is
not a piece — it is a seam, and it belongs to the coherence pass.
3. `brief` states what EXISTS today and what is MISSING, concretely. Vague
briefs produce vague work; every brief below names a measurement or a
4. `shots` names states from the review sheet. A piece whose shots do not
show its work will be judged on something else.

project.name: EXAMPLE
observe: node tools/capture.mjs                      full review sheet -> shots/
rules: The quality bar is <BENCHMARK>. Not "good for a side project". If the team that shipped <BENCHMARK> would flag it, it is not done.

STRICT FILE OWNERSHIP. Only edit the files in your brief. Other agents are editing other files right now. Touching a file you do not own gets reverted and wastes the round. Need a change elsewhere? Say so in your report.
Deterministic: seeded RNG, frozen clock, no wall-clock reads in logic that decides outcomes.
Never break the harness — every reviewer drives the product through it, so breaking it makes your work unjudgeable.
No new runtime dependencies without saying so in your report.
project.state: Describe honestly where the project is today, in three or four sentences. Every builder and every critic reads this, so a stale one costs a round.

pieces.name: The list view
pieces.brief: Own the primary list. It renders rows and nothing else: no grouping, no keyboard navigation, no empty state, no density control. Build grouping by any column with sticky group headers; full keyboard navigation including range select; a real empty state that tells the user what to do next rather than showing a shrug; and a loading state that reserves layout so the page does not jump. It must stay readable at 500 rows and at 3 rows.

pieces.name: The detail pane
pieces.brief: Own the detail pane. Describe what exists and what is missing, concretely.

pieces.name: Performance
pieces.brief: Own the frame and payload budget. Measure first, then cut — do not guess at what is expensive. Add whatever counters you need to the harness's stats(). Hard constraint: nothing you do may change a single observable output. Prove it — run the same fixture at two quality levels and diff the snapshots.
